direct_sign_mode_transaction.note: SIGN_MODE_DIRECT with an eth_secp256k1 account key. sign_doc_bytes is the protobuf SignDoc {body_bytes, auth_info_bytes, chain_id, account_number}; the signature covers keccak256(sign_doc_bytes), not SHA-256, and is exactly 64 bytes R||S with low S. The 65-byte form some Ethereum signers return is rejected on this path. The transaction carries no extension option; a Web3 extension option selects the EIP-712 path of msg_create_session_transaction instead. The public key is the account key of this file, packed as an Any of pubkey_type_url, and must be the compressed 33-byte point stored on the account. request_auth_negative_cases_format: Each row changes one thing about its base section. "signed" is what the signer signed: the named key over the base message and domain with the listed member overrides, and signature_65 is that exact RFC 6979 signature. "verified" is what the verifier rebuilds, as overrides of the base; signing_digest is that digest and recovered_address is what the signature (the row's, or the base section's when the row has no "signed") recovers to over it. A row with verification_context is a session-grant window decision at that height, from the base grant expiryHeight. expect is the verifier outcome; error, where present, is the Ingress error code, and status, where present, the gRPC status. The verifier runs five steps in order and stops at the first failure, which fixes the code: (1) format - lowercase-hex ids, a 32-byte nonce, an expiry above zero, an OpenTask expiry that is a chain height (below 10^12) rather than Unix milliseconds, endpoint matching method, the derived OpenTask task_id and payload_ref, a signer_address and OpenTask user_address in canonical lowercase trueopen Bech32 that decode to exactly 20 bytes, a projectable body - NEXUS_INGRESS_MALFORMED; (2) with a grant, a method outside the session-allowed set (and on the Task data path a non-OUTPUT object) - SDK_AUTH_SESSION_METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED or DATA_ACCESS_SESSION_METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED; (3) the grant chain, user, user signature or stored account key - ..._SESSION_GRANT_INVALID, and the grant window - ..._SESSION_GRANT_EXPIRED; (4) the request signature, rebuilt with the sessionGrantHash the verifier derives and with the verifier's own chain_id and evm_chain_id, never the request's - SDK_AUTH_INVALID_SIGNATURE or DATA_ACCESS_INVALID_SIGNATURE, which also covers a wrong derived grant hash, a request signed for another chain (sdk_request_other_chain_id), a chain_id field other than the verifier's own (rejected here even though it could be detected at the format step), a wrong domain chainId, a version 1 signature and, for a wallet-signed request, an account that is missing, has no stored key or has a stored key other than the recovered one; (5) on SDKRequestEnvelopeV2, request expiry - SDK_AUTH_EXPIRED - and replay - SDK_AUTH_REPLAY; on TaskDataRequestAuthV1, a builder_operator_address other than the verifying Builder - DATA_ACCESS_DENIED - then request expiry - NEXUS_DATA_EXPIRED - then replay, then the Task duty - DATA_ACCESS_DENIED. The replay key uses the verifier's own chain_id. ConfirmOpenTask is refused before these steps with FailedPrecondition and NEXUS_INGRESS_CONTRACT_NOT_FROZEN. A row with none of signed, verified or verification_context is a rule stated in prose; its transport column, where present, shows the offending transport value, which is rejected before any typed data exists. tools/verify-vector-consistency recomputes every published value.

sdk_request.contract: SDK request typed-data signing (SDKRequestEnvelopeV2), wallet signed
sdk_request.encode_type: SDKRequest(string chainId,string method,string endpoint,bytes32 sessionId,bytes32 taskId,bytes32 requestNonce,uint64 expiryHeightOrTime,bytes32 bodyDigest,bytes32 sessionGrantHash)
sdk_request.note: OpenTask, signed by the user wallet directly; OpenTask never accepts a session grant. sessionGrantHash is 32 zero bytes because no grant is attached; the verifier derives it and never reads it from the request. expiryHeightOrTime below 10^12 is a chain height, which only OpenTask may use; OpenTask accepts only a chain height, and a Unix millisecond expiry is NEXUS_INGRESS_MALFORMED at the format step. The signature must recover to signer_address, which must equal the order user, and the recovered public key must equal the account's stored key. method is the bare method name and endpoint the full procedure /nexus.v1.IngressAPI/<Method>, whose <Method> must equal method. session_id and task_id travel as 64-character lowercase hex without 0x, are decoded strictly and enter as bytes32; any other spelling is rejected before projection. For OpenTask task_id must equal TRUEOPEN_TASK_ID_V1(session_id, order_sequence), here order sequence 7. requestNonce is exactly 32 bytes, and an expiry of 0 or below is rejected before projection. The user account must already hold its public key on chain (it has submitted MsgCreateSession). request_domain, signer_address, signature and the deprecated signer_pubkey are not typed fields. The replay_key column spells the NUL separators as \x00. Timing assumed by the expected results (fixture material, not network values): max_session_grant_blocks = 400, max_service_material_expiry_blocks = 604800 (the ServiceParamsV1 value in params_v1.json; any value of 800 or more gives the same results), request_ttl_blocks = 20. This OpenTask row expires at chain height 1010 and assumes current_height 1000; any height from 990 to 1010 accepts it, since an OpenTask height expiry must satisfy current_height <= expiry <= current_height + request_ttl_blocks. It is evaluated separately from the session rows, whose grant needs a height from 1100 to 1500.

sdk_request_session.contract: SDK request typed-data signing (SDKRequestEnvelopeV2), session-key signed
sdk_request_session.encode_type: SDKRequest(string chainId,string method,string endpoint,bytes32 sessionId,bytes32 taskId,bytes32 requestNonce,uint64 expiryHeightOrTime,bytes32 bodyDigest,bytes32 sessionGrantHash)
sdk_request_session.note: SubscribeOutput signed by the session key under the grant of session_grant. sessionGrantHash is that grant's hash_struct. The signature recovers to the grant's sessionKey, and is compared with it only; the grant carries the account check. signer_address stays the granting user and keys the replay record. expiryHeightOrTime of 10^12 or more is Unix milliseconds, the only form methods other than OpenTask accept. Timing assumed by the expected results (fixture material, not network values): max_session_grant_blocks = 400, max_service_material_expiry_blocks = 604800 (the ServiceParamsV1 value in params_v1.json; any value of 800 or more gives the same results), request_ttl_blocks = 20. It assumes current_height 1200, inside the grant window of session_grant, and a verifier clock at or before the Unix-millisecond expiry 1790000000000. request_ttl_blocks does not apply: only an OpenTask expiry is a chain height.

session_grant.encode_type: SessionGrant(string chainId,string user,address sessionKey,uint64 expiryHeight,bytes32 grantNonce)
session_grant.note: Signed once by the user wallet under the SDK Request domain. sessionKey is the EIP-712 address of the session_key test key (a wallet JSON spells it 0x-prefixed); it is not an on-chain account. user_signature must recover to user, and user must be an existing account whose stored public key equals the recovered one. A request carrying this grant binds it through sessionGrantHash = hash_struct. verification_context is fixture material, not a network parameter: max_session_grant_blocks is a deployment value, and the rule is current_height <= expiryHeight <= current_height + max_session_grant_blocks with checked addition. There is no revocation; the grant is reusable until it expires and is not a replay record of its own. Timing assumed by the expected results (fixture material, not network values): max_session_grant_blocks = 400, max_service_material_expiry_blocks = 604800 (the ServiceParamsV1 value in params_v1.json; any value of 800 or more gives the same results), request_ttl_blocks = 20. The grant (expiryHeight 1500) and the session rows built on it assume current_height 1200, as verification_context states: 1200 <= 1500 <= 1200 + 400. The grant-window rows in request_auth_negative_cases each state their own current_height with max_session_grant_blocks 400: 1501 and 1099 reject, 1100 and 1500 accept.

session_key.note: Deterministic session-key test material. The session key is generated by the client and held in memory only; it is not an account, so it has no Bech32 form.

task_data_request.contract: Task data request typed-data signing (TaskDataRequestAuthV1 USER path), version 2, wallet signed
task_data_request.encode_type: TaskDataRequest(uint32 schemaVersion,string chainId,string builderOperatorAddress,string rpcMethod,bytes32 bodyDigest,uint32 requesterKind,string requesterAddress,uint64 serviceAuthorizationNonce,bytes32 requestNonce,uint64 expiryHeight,bytes32 sessionGrantHash)
task_data_request.note: The USER branch of TaskDataRequestAuthV1 under domain version 2. Typed fields 1-10 project auth fields 1-10 and sessionGrantHash is 32 zero bytes without a grant. requester_kind alone selects the verifier: USER signs this typed data and supplies exactly 65 bytes, CORTEX_SERVICE signs the TRUEOPEN_TASK_DATA_REQUEST_V1 H_FIELDS_V1 digest and supplies exactly 64. Neither length is sniffed and no caller pubkey is trusted. personal_sign, eth_sign and raw64 are rejected, a USER request carries serviceAuthorizationNonce 0, and domain version 1 is not accepted. Timing assumed by the expected results (fixture material, not network values): max_session_grant_blocks = 400, max_service_material_expiry_blocks = 604800 (the ServiceParamsV1 value in params_v1.json; any value of 800 or more gives the same results), request_ttl_blocks = 20. It assumes current_height 1200, so expiryHeight 2000 is inside current_height <= expiry_height <= current_height + max_service_material_expiry_blocks.

task_data_request_session.contract: Task data request typed-data signing (TaskDataRequestAuthV1 USER path), version 2, session-key signed
task_data_request_session.encode_type: TaskDataRequest(uint32 schemaVersion,string chainId,string builderOperatorAddress,string rpcMethod,bytes32 bodyDigest,uint32 requesterKind,string requesterAddress,uint64 serviceAuthorizationNonce,bytes32 requestNonce,uint64 expiryHeight,bytes32 sessionGrantHash)
task_data_request_session.note: GetTaskDataMetadata of an OUTPUT object, signed by the session key under the grant of session_grant, which is signed in the SDK Request domain. The grant is checked as for an SDK request with requester_address in place of signer_address; the signature recovers to the grant's sessionKey. Only GetTaskDataMetadata and FetchTaskData of an OUTPUT object accept a grant. The grant is always signed under the SDK Request domain, never under this one. Timing assumed by the expected results (fixture material, not network values): max_session_grant_blocks = 400, max_service_material_expiry_blocks = 604800 (the ServiceParamsV1 value in params_v1.json; any value of 800 or more gives the same results), request_ttl_blocks = 20. It assumes current_height 1200: the grant (expiryHeight 1500) is inside 1200 <= 1500 <= 1200 + 400, and the request (expiryHeight 2000) is inside current_height <= expiry_height <= current_height + max_service_material_expiry_blocks, which at height 1200 needs max_service_material_expiry_blocks of at least 800. request_ttl_blocks does not apply to Task data requests.

task_data_request_v1_obsolete.contract: Task data request typed-data signing, domain version 1 (obsolete)
task_data_request_v1_obsolete.encode_type: TaskDataRequest(uint32 schemaVersion,string chainId,string builderOperatorAddress,string rpcMethod,bytes32 bodyDigest,uint32 requesterKind,string requesterAddress,uint64 serviceAuthorizationNonce,bytes32 requestNonce,uint64 expiryHeight)
task_data_request_v1_obsolete.note: Domain version 1, without sessionGrantHash, has no fresh-genesis route: a verifier must reject this signature. It is kept, with its values unchanged, as a negative vector; task_data_request is the version 2 replacement. The USER branch of TaskDataRequestAuthV1. requester_kind alone selects the verifier: USER signs this EIP-712 v4 typed data and supplies exactly 65 bytes, CORTEX_SERVICE signs the TRUEOPEN_TASK_DATA_REQUEST_V1 H_FIELDS_V1 digest and supplies exactly 64. Neither length is sniffed and no caller pubkey is trusted. personal_sign, eth_sign and raw64 are rejected on the USER path, and a USER request must carry serviceAuthorizationNonce 0.
